title: Stacked townhouse rezoning approved for St. David Street North
subtitle: Operations centre design, compensation review, HR sharing with Puslinch, Trade Tracks fee relief and rescue training access.
overview: Council approved a zoning change for 950 and 960 St. David Street North in Fergus, allowing a rebuilt "new to you" store and stacked townhouses behind it {{vote:m6}}. An amendment added a requirement for ground-level, secure, indoor bicycle storage at roughly 15-25% of the total parking requirement {{vote:m5}}. Concerns about traffic, parking, garbage handling and active transportation will be worked through at site plan stage.

Council also endorsed adding Planning & Development to the new Township Operations Centre, with staff to report back on alternatives, including future use of the house {{vote:m3}}. It awarded a compensation market review that includes a review of Council remuneration {{vote:m9}}, and approved a fee-for-service human resources agreement with Puslinch {{vote:m11}}.

Other decisions included partial rental fee relief for the Trade Tracks event {{vote:m12}}, a part lot control exemption for semi-detached homes in Storybrook {{vote:m7}}, and a training access agreement allowing fire rescue to use Grand River Conservation Authority lands {{vote:m13}}. Council also chose two members for the advisory committee selection team by lottery {{vote:m10}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved application RZ11/22 and gave three readings to the zoning amendment, with a condition requiring secure indoor bicycle storage in the final site plan.
Council endorsed conceptual design Option 2 to add Planning & Development and directed staff to report back on alternatives, including the future use of the house, before detail design.
Council awarded RFP #02-23 to Marianne Love Consulting at an upset limit of $41,550 and approved the provisional Council remuneration review at an added $4,800, both before HST.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign a fee-for-service agreement to provide HR services to Puslinch, replacing the shared position.
Council directed staff to remove the ball diamond and soccer field charges, saving $896.07, and to block off those spaces during the event.
Council approved the selection team structure and appointed Councillors Jefferson and Evoy to it.
Council received an overview of the system and endorsed the Quality Management System Operational Plan.
Council approved several items including a Walser Building holding zone removal, a bridge weight restriction by-law, and a paving collaboration on Eighth Line West.

debate: On the St. David Street rezoning, councillors raised traffic spillover, sidewalk and active transportation connections, play space, and how garbage would be stored and collected for the residential units. The applicant's consultant said these would be addressed at site plan.

Some councillors asked whether any of the townhouses would be affordable or attainable. The consultant said they would not be considered affordable. Staff said provincial policy is market-driven and does not require affordable units in every development.

On the bicycle storage amendment, staff said the zoning by-law does not require bicycle parking and that it is only encouraged in guidelines. They questioned whether it could be legally required, but the amendment passed.

On the compensation review, staff cited difficulty recruiting for hard-to-fill positions and pay equity compliance. One councillor argued flexible work options should be offered to managers, and another asked why the Council remuneration review was being done now. Staff said it was cheaper to combine it with the staff review.

On Trade Tracks, staff said past councils have not waived fees and that fees offset venue costs. They suggested removing only the unused buffer space as a one-time measure for the first event. Councillors also asked whether the 15% large-event discount should extend to smaller groups.
